d25d7ec96e.q: How many hours per year can construction leaders lose to workplace interruptions and what causes attention residue?
d25d7ec96e.a: A project manager named Daniel tracked his time for one week and found he was spending three hours a day on interruptions from other people. Multiplying three hours a day across 220 working days equals 660 hours per year—more than 16 forty-hour work weeks. Sophie Leroy, who studies how people focus at work, found that when you switch from one task to another, part of your mind stays stuck on the last task, which she calls attention residue. Every interruption costs you not only the time it takes but also the focus you do not get back right away.

0aa4b0f608.q: What is time blocking and what are the three main types of blocks that do most of the work?
0aa4b0f608.a: Time blocking means giving every hour a job before the week starts so your inbox and interruptions do not control your calendar. The three blocks that do most of the work are: a focus block, which is 90 minutes on a Box One priority with the door closed, alerts off, and your phone on the other side of the room; office hours, which are set two times a day when your people know they can find you and bring their issues to you; and a buffer of 60 minutes a day with nothing in it because something always goes sideways on a job site. 02c2794a1c.q: How long does it take to regain focus after an interruption according to research?

This research demonstrates why protecting time blocks and minimizing interruptions is critical for construction leaders' productivity.
